claims.claim: Query-probe disagreement in GPT2-XL and GPT-J is mostly explained by confabulation and heterogeneity; confident-contradiction 'deception' cases are rare except on CREAK.
claims.stance_target: probe-vs-output gap reflects calibration/uncertainty rather than lying
claims.scope_conditions: BoolQ, SciQ, CREAK; GPT2-XL, GPT-J; linear probes
claims.quoted_support: In many cases, the superiority of probes is simply attributable to better calibration on uncertain answers rather than a greater fraction of correct, high-confidence answers.

claims.claim: Probes beat queries in accuracy (GPT-J: BoolQ 62.5 vs 61.8, SciQ 88.6 vs 84.1, CREAK 71.0 vs 50.4) and are substantially better calibrated.
claims.quoted_support: Probes are well calibrated, while queries are reasonably well calibrated on SciQ but poorly calibrated on other datasets.

claims.claim: Ensembling probe and query probabilities improves accuracy in 4 of 6 cases (SciQ GPT-J 90.5, CREAK GPT-J 71.3).
claims.stance_target: probe and output readouts are complementary
claims.scope_conditions: lambda chosen on 500 validation examples per dataset, Eq. 1
claims.quoted_support: Surprisingly, by ensembling probes and queries together, it is possible in 4 of 6 cases to obtain further improvements.

claims.claim: A fine-tuned GPT2-XL queried directly beats probing the pretrained model on SciQ (+6.9%) and CREAK (+4.0%), so probe superiority partly reflects many-shot training of probes versus zero-shot queries.
claims.stance_target: probe advantage is partly a supervision confound
claims.quoted_support: Probe predictions exhibited 1.7% better accuracy than fine-tuned model queries on BoolQ. However, querying the fine-tuned model had 6.9% and 4.0% better accuracy on SciQ and CREAK.

breadth.confidence_families: Linear hidden-state probe p_probe(correct|h) versus direct query probability p_LM(a|q) (Section 2 Extracting answers from LMs); ensemble of the two (Eq. 1, Section 5). No verbal or sampling consistency.
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: GPT2-XL and GPT-J (Section 3 Models); autoregressive LMs only.
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: instruct, RLHF, chat); only pretrained base LMs plus one fine-tuned GPT2-XL control (Section 3).
breadth.post_training_stages: not present beyond a supervised fine-tune of GPT2-XL on true QA pairs (Section 3 end); no RLHF/DPO.
breadth.reasoning_models: not present (searched: reasoning, chain-of-thought, thinking); reasoning not enabled, models are GPT2-XL/GPT-J.
breadth.elicitation_formats: Query: rank yes/no or answers by p_LM(a|q); probe: final-layer hidden state of [q,a] (Section 2, Section 3 Probes). Footnote 3: alternative query formats tried with 'no striking changes'.
breadth.benchmarks: BoolQ, SciQ (one distractor retained), CREAK (Section 3 Datasets); all factual QA, no code.
breadth.label_source: Dataset gold labels for correctness; probes trained on train splits (Section 3 Probes).
breadth.label_independence: Train/test splits of each dataset; ensemble lambda on 500 validation examples (Section 5). No grouped independence analysis.
breadth.contamination_split: not present (searched: contamination, pretraining overlap, release date).
breadth.calibration_metrics: Calibration plot of confidence vs empirical accuracy for GPT-J (Figure 2); accuracy (Table 1); probe entropy / query confidence taxonomy (Figure 1, 3). No ECE/Brier number reported (searched: ECE, Brier).
breadth.causal_intervention: not present (searched: steering, ablation, patching). Footnote 4 cautions a successful probe does not show the LM uses the feature.
